note: Steps, then a 3rd: a tune that starts on Re, learned in named stages (with the tune, Tune muted, Chords muted), then a tune that opens with a skip from Do to Mi and moves on by step. The old Key selector is now moves (any key, 40 to 60 bpm), with the line about another key marked {{?key}}; both tunes start at a beginner's 40, and the why says what makes the two moves different.

exercise.title: Steps, then 3rds
exercise.why: A step moves to the next note of the scale and a 3rd skips one, so once your voice knows both distances it can sing most of the moves a tune makes.

cells.text:
Press Play below to hear the tune at {{=bpm}}: the mic starts with it. This tune starts on Re, one step above Do. Sing along on the note names.
Sing along with the tune a few times. Then press Tune below to mute the tune, and sing it over the chords alone.
Once you find Re without the tune, press Chords to mute the chords too, and sing the tune a cappella.
{{?key}}In another key the notes change, but the tune still starts one step above Do.

Press Play below to hear the tune: the mic starts with it. The tune opens with a skip from Do to Mi, then moves by step. Sing along on "oo".
Practice until the skip and the steps feel as different as they sound.
